paper_title: Reducing Trap Density in Organic Solar Cells via Extending the Fused Ring Donor Unit of an A-D-A-Type Nonfullerene Acceptor for Over 17% Efficiency
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2022 - Zhou - Reducing Trap Density in Organic Solar Cells via Extending the Fused Ring Donor Unit of/auto/Advanced Materials - 2022 - Zhou - Reducing Trap Density in Organic Solar Cells via Extending the Fused Ring Donor Unit of.md

knowledge_points.content: Extending the donor core of an A-D-A-type nonfullerene acceptor from a heptacyclic unit (BTPIC-4F) to a nonacyclic unit (TTPIC-4F) enhances intramolecular and intermolecular interactions.
knowledge_points.evidence: In this study, the trap density in OSCs is efficiently reduced via extending the donor core of nonfullerene acceptors (NFAs) from a heptacyclic unit to a nonacyclic unit. TTPIC-4F with a nonacyclic unit has stronger intramolecular and intermolecular interactions.

knowledge_points.content: The D18:TTPIC-4F-based organic solar cell achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 17.1%, which is significantly higher than the 10.3% PCE of the D18:BTPIC-4F-based device.
knowledge_points.evidence: the D18:TTPIC-4F-based OSC achieves a much superior PCE of 17.1% ... compared with the D18:BTPIC-4F-based OSC (PCE = 10.3%).

knowledge_points.content: The TTPIC-4F molecule possesses a smaller dihedral angle between the donor unit and end groups (5.4°) compared to BTPIC-4F (21.5°), facilitating a shorter S···O distance (2.69 Å) and improved molecular planarity.
knowledge_points.evidence: The dihedral angle between the donor unit and the end groups of TTPIC-4F is 5.4°, which is significantly smaller than that of BTPIC-4F (21.5°). ... The shorter S···O distance for TTPIC-4F can afford stronger intramolecular noncovalent interactions to sustain the planarity.

knowledge_points.content: The total trap density of the D18:TTPIC-4F device, calculated using the space-charge-limited-current (SCLC) method, is 4.02 × 10^15 cm⁻³, which is among the lowest reported for organic semiconductors.
knowledge_points.evidence: the total trap density in the D18:TTPIC-4F-based device was calculated to be 4.02 × 10^15 cm⁻³, which is lower than that in the D18:BTPIC-4F-based device (1.06 × 10^16 cm⁻³).

knowledge_points.content: First-principles quantum-mechanical calculations show that TTPIC-4F has a maximum electronic coupling (transfer integral) of 19.14 meV, nearly an order of magnitude higher than BTPIC-4F (2.46 meV).
knowledge_points.evidence: The maximum electronic coupling for electrons of the TTPIC-4F crystal is 19.14 meV, which is almost one order higher than that of the BTPIC-4F crystal (2.46 meV).

knowledge_points.content: The D18:TTPIC-4F blend film exhibits a lower root-mean-square roughness of 1.11 nm compared to 2.30 nm for D18:BTPIC-4F, which aids in efficient charge-carrier collection.
knowledge_points.evidence: the root-mean-square roughness of the D18:TTPIC-4F blend film is 1.11 nm and smaller than that of the D18:BTPIC-4F blend film (2.30 nm).

knowledge_points.content: Fourier-transform photocurrent spectroscopy external quantum efficiency (FTPS-EQE) reveals that TTPIC-4F-based devices have a lower Urbach energy (21.7 meV) than BTPIC-4F-based devices (26.8 meV), indicating reduced energetic disorder.
knowledge_points.evidence: By fitting the FTPS-EQE onset, the D18:TTPIC-4F-based device exhibited a lower Urbach energy (21.7 meV) than the D18:BTPIC-4F-based device (26.8 meV).

knowledge_points.content: The electron and hole mobilities in D18:TTPIC-4F devices are 4.31 × 10⁻⁴ and 2.20 × 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, respectively, which are nearly ten times higher than those in BTPIC-4F devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: the electron and hole mobilities of the D18:TTPIC-4F-based devices are 4.31 × 10⁻⁴ and 2.20 × 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, respectively, and almost one order of magnitude higher than those of D18:BTPIC-4F-based devices.

knowledge_points.content: Thermal admittance spectroscopy (TAS) measurements confirm that the D18:TTPIC-4F-based device has a lower trap density of states (tDOS) than the BTPIC-4F counterpart within the energy depth of 0.15–0.23 eV.
knowledge_points.evidence: According to the TAS results (Figure 4c), the D18:TTPIC-4F-based device exhibits a lower trap density of states (tDOS) of 3.5–6.0 × 10^15 cm⁻³ eV⁻¹ than the D18:BTPIC-4F-based device (0.4–1.2 × 10^16 cm⁻³ eV⁻¹).
